You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of freytag-forge; edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. You own ONLY storygame/runtime/command_split.py, the NEW file tests/test_command_split_negation.py, and the NEW notes file /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage5-notes/corpus-engine-path.md. Touch nothing else; never remove or weaken an existing assertion (tests/test_command_split.py must pass unchanged). Never run anything billed.

BUG (verified by running it). RuntimeEngine._turn_active (storygame/runtime/engine.py ~line 247) runs command_text = ' '.join(split_command(player_input)) and hands command_text to the provider. storygame/runtime/command_split.py::split_command uses a spaCy parse to split coordinated imperatives. For 'Open the drawer, but do not take anything yet.' it returns ['Open the drawer, but do not.', 'Take anything yet.']: the negated coordinated verb 'take' (under 'do not') is treated as a separate action, which (1) strands 'but do not.' on the first piece and (2) turns the player's restraint into the positive command 'Take anything yet.' The same happens for 'Search Brandon's hideout for leaked documents, but do not copy anything yet.' and 'Check the copied JANUS files, but do not send anything yet.' (the three restraint entries in tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json). Consequence on staging: storygame.runtime.candidate_matcher.negation_scoped_command (read it; it lets an unrelated trailing restraint clause through) never sees the intact sentence, so the restraint commands earn nothing even though matcher-level tests pass. 'Open the drawer; do not take anything yet.' (semicolon) is not split, which is why the earlier engine test passed.

FIX. In command_split.py, do not treat a NEGATED coordinated verb as a split point. In _coordinated_verbs (or in the caller), skip any candidate verb whose subtree contains a negation: a token with dep_ == 'neg', or the lowercase text in {'not', "n't", 'never', 'no', 'without'}, or an aux child of the candidate that itself carries such a negation. When a candidate is skipped, also skip the conjuncts chained under it. Verbs that are not negated must split exactly as before. Result: the three restraint commands above and 'Open the drawer, but don't take anything yet.' and 'Open the drawer and do not take anything.' come back as ONE piece, unchanged. 'Open the drawer and take the key.' still splits into 2 pieces and 'Open the drawer, take the key, then search the room.' into 3. Mixed case 'Open the drawer and take the key, but don't search the room.' may split into ['Open the drawer.', "Take the key, but don't search the room."]; assert only that no piece starts with a positive imperative of the negated verb ('Search the room.' must never appear as its own piece).

TESTS in tests/test_command_split_negation.py (offline, hermetic): a parametrized table of the unsplit cases above and the still-split cases; the mixed case; the exact bug strings (assert the old output ['Open the drawer, but do not.', 'Take anything yet.'] is no longer produced); and an ENGINE-LEVEL test through RuntimeEngine in scene 1A with the COMMA form 'Open the drawer, but do not take anything yet.' that earns k_sl_1a_f_r1 (copy the provider/engine helper style of tests/test_negation_scope.py, its _provider and _scene_1a_state helpers; do not edit that file), plus 'Do not open the drawer.' and 'Open the drawer, never mind.' earning nothing through the same engine path. Confirm the new unsplit and engine-level tests fail on the old command_split.py (git stash the source file) and say so in your final message.

CORPUS ENGINE-PATH NOTE (also required). Write /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage5-notes/corpus-engine-path.md: for EVERY entry in tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json, compute what the real engine would match, i.e. run ' '.join(split_command(entry['input'])) through the same scene candidates and matcher call tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py uses (read it), and list every entry whose engine-path result differs from its recorded `observed` (id, input, split pieces, observed, engine-path result). After your fix the three restraint entries must agree. Do NOT edit the corpus fixture or its test; the note is the deliverable. If the note shows other differing entries, list them plainly; do not try to fix them.

HOW TO RUN. First confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside this worktree. Iterate with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_command_split.py tests/test_command_split_negation.py tests/test_negation_scope.py tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py`, then the whole `tests` directory, and ruff check / ruff format --check (line length 120) via /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/ruff on your two files.

COMPLETION RULE: do not stop until the fix, tests and the corpus note exist, the full suite is green and ruff is clean. Finish by listing files changed and pasting the pytest summary and the differing-entry list from the note.
